scenes.headline: How a fourth projection lets attention prefetch its cache
scenes.sub: SparDA: sparse attention that picks the next layer's KV blocks one layer early.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lotus! Sparse attention reads only a few blocks of the KV cache. SparDA picks the next layer's blocks early, so fetching them hides behind compute.

scenes.text: A fourth projection, the Forecast, selects the next layer's KV blocks from this one, so they can cross from CPU memory while this layer still computes.
scenes.say: The idea: a fourth projection, the Forecast, picks the next layer's blocks from this one. So they can come over from CPU memory while this layer still computes.

steps.say: Each layer's projection now emits a fourth tensor next to Q, K and V: the Forecast.
The Forecast scores the next layer's compressed keys and picks its top blocks, before this layer has even attended.

steps.note: decode only: in prefill every key is already on the GPU
steps.say: In decode, the cache lives in CPU memory, and those blocks start crossing PCIe at once, on a separate stream,
while this layer's attention and FFN run. When the next layer needs its blocks, they've usually arrived.

left.title: Baseline selector
items: Every query head in a group scores every block
Sum the scores, softmax, then top-k
left.say: The usual selector has every query head in a group score every block, then sums and normalizes. At long context, that can cost more than attention.

right.title: Forecast indexer
right.say: The Forecast uses one head per GQA group, and no softmax. That's why prefill speeds up too, where nothing needs fetching.

scenes.title: Decode at 128K, tokens per second
scenes.note: MiniCPM4.1-8B; without offload, nothing past batch 4 fits
scenes.say: Offloading lets the batch grow; the Forecast hides the fetch. The headline five point three times compares different batch sizes, so check the baseline.

scenes.text: Selection needn't wait for the query. Decided one layer ahead, it becomes a prefetch, as good as the selector it copies.
scenes.say: So selection doesn't have to wait for the query. Moved one layer ahead, it becomes a prefetch, trained to copy the selector it replaces.

recap: A fourth projection picks the next layer's blocks
Their transfer overlaps this layer's compute
One head per group: selection gets cheaper too
scenes.say: To recap: pick one layer early, fetch while computing, and select with one head per group.
